data.name: Himanta
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘हिमान्त’ (Himanta), meaning ‘mighty’, ‘powerful’ or ‘terrific’. This name is associated with the mighty god, Lord Indra, who is known as the king of the gods and the god of rain, thunderbolts, and the sky in Hindu mythology.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes power, strength, and resilience. It is believed that those named Himanta are blessed with the divine grace of Lord Indra, who bestows upon them the courage and determination to overcome any challenge they may face in life.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Himavat, in Hindu mythology, personified as a mountain king and the father of the Himalayas. The name Himanta carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Himavat is an important figure in Hindu mythology, often considered the father of the Himalayas. This name is derived from 'Himavat', possibly referring to snow or ice.

historical_references.reference: According to the Mahabharata, Himanta was a king in ancient India, a descendant of Himalaya and the father of the Pandava prince Bhima.
historical_references.context: Himanta is also mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata as a king and the father of Bhima, the second Pandava brother. He is described as a powerful and fearsome ruler, and a descendant of the mountains.

This name is therefore associated with the power and purity of the mountains and the divine energy they represent.
